subject: ss-cardiology
title: Cardiology
curriculum: NMC Competency-Based DM Cardiology Curriculum / NBEMS NEET-SS Cardiology Specialty Group
examPattern: NEET-SS Cardiology (100% General Medicine feeder and Cardiology subspecialty: invasive/non-invasive hemodynamics, electrophysiology, acute and chronic coronary syndromes, structural and valvular heart disease, heart failure and mechanical circulatory support, congenital heart disease, vascular medicine and preventive cardiology).
book: Braunwald's Heart Disease: A Textbook of Cardiovascular Medicine 12th Edition; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22nd Edition

topics.title: Cardiac physiology and haemodynamics
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 22, 23 (Hemodynamic Principles)

mustKnow.fact: Frank-Starling law dictates that myocardial stroke volume increases in proportion to end-diastolic volume within physiological sarcomere lengths of 1.8 to 2.2 micrometres.
Cardiac output equals heart rate multiplied by stroke volume, with a normal resting cardiac index ranging from 2.6 to 4.2 L/min/m2.

Myocardial oxygen consumption is determined by wall stress, heart rate, and contractility as quantified by the Law of Laplace where stress equals pressure times radius divided by twice wall thickness.
Ventricular compliance is represented by the slope of the end-diastolic pressure-volume relationship, where decreased compliance elevates diastolic filling pressures.

Force-frequency relationship or Bowditch staircase phenomenon describes an intrinsic increase in myocardial contractility as heart rate rises due to calcium accumulation in the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
Coronary blood flow to the left ventricle occurs predominantly during diastole because intramyocardial tissue pressure during systole compresses intramural vessels.
Anrep effect describes the transient inotropic autoregulation of ventricular myocardium following an acute increase in afterload.
Normal left ventricular ejection fraction measured by echocardiography or ventriculography is 50% to 70%, reflecting fractional volume ejected during systole.

topics.title: Electrocardiography
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 14 (Electrocardiography)

mustKnow.fact: Normal PR interval ranges from 120 to 200 ms, reflecting conduction time through the atria, atrioventricular node, and His-Purkinje system.
Normal QRS duration is less than 120 ms, where widening beyond 120 ms signifies intraventricular conduction delay or bundle branch block.
Corrected QT interval (QTc) calculated by Bazett formula is prolonged when exceeding 450 ms in adult men and 460 ms in adult women.
Sokolow-Lyon index for left ventricular hypertrophy requires the sum of S wave in V1 and R wave in V5 or V6 to exceed 35 mm.
Cornell voltage criteria defines left ventricular hypertrophy when R wave in aVL plus S wave in V3 exceeds 28 mm in men or 20 mm in women.
Wellens syndrome type A demonstrates biphasic T waves in leads V2 and V3, while type B demonstrates deep symmetric inverted T waves signalling critical proximal LAD stenosis.
De Winter pattern demonstrates upsloping ST-segment depression at the J-point in precordial leads with tall prominent symmetric T waves representing acute LAD occlusion without ST elevation.
Brugada type 1 ECG pattern features coved ST-segment elevation of 2 mm or greater in right precordial leads followed by a negative T wave.

topics.title: Echocardiography and cardiac imaging
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 16, 17 (Echocardiography, CMR, Cardiac CT)

mustKnow.fact: E/e ratio on tissue Doppler imaging correlates with left ventricular filling pressures, where an average E/e ratio greater than 14 indicates elevated left atrial pressure.
Global longitudinal strain by speckle-tracking echocardiography detects early subclinical myocardial dysfunction, with normal values typically more negative than -18% to -20%.
Agatston coronary artery calcium score by noncontrast cardiac CT quantifies atherosclerotic calcification, where a score over 400 denotes high cardiovascular risk.
Cardiac magnetic resonance late gadolinium enhancement allows differentiation between ischemic transmural infarction and nonischemic midwall or subepicardial fibrosis patterns.
Myocardial extracellular volume fraction measured on cardiac MRI T1 mapping exceeds 30% in diffuse interstitial fibrosis and rises above 40% in cardiac amyloidosis.
Continuity equation in echocardiography calculates aortic valve area based on conservation of mass where stroke volume through the LVOT equals flow through the stenotic orifice.
PISA method (proximal isovelocity surface area) calculates regurgitant orifice area and regurgitant volume based on hemispheric flow convergence toward the regurgitant orifice.
Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) possesses a high negative predictive value of 97% to 99% for ruling out obstructive coronary artery disease in low-to-intermediate risk patients.

topics.title: Cardiac catheterisation and invasive haemodynamics
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 21, 22 (Coronary Angiography and Invasive Hemodynamics)

mustKnow.fact: Fick principle calculates cardiac output by dividing total body oxygen consumption by the arteriovenous oxygen content difference across the pulmonary circulation.
Thermodilution technique measures cardiac output via a pulmonary artery catheter by measuring temperature change downstream following injection of cold saline.
Normal mean pulmonary capillary wedge pressure ranges between 6 and 12 mmHg, serving as an indirect surrogate for left atrial and left ventricular end-diastolic pressure.
Gorlin formula calculates stenotic valve orifice area by dividing transvalvular flow rate by the square root of mean transvalvular pressure gradient multiplied by an empirical constant.
Fractional flow reserve (FFR) evaluates lesion-specific ischemia, where an FFR value of 0.80 or less during maximal adenosine hyperemia indicates hemodynamically significant stenosis.
Instantaneous wave-free ratio (iFR) evaluates coronary stenosis severity during the wave-free period of diastole without requiring vasodilator administration, with a diagnostic cutoff of 0.89.
Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) minimum lumen area (MLA) threshold indicating hemodynamically significant left main coronary stenosis is 4.5 to 6.0 mm2.

Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides high spatial resolution of 10 to 15 micrometres, ideal for assessing stent apposition, neoatherosclerosis, and fibrous cap thickness in thin-cap fibroatheroma.

topics.title: Atherosclerosis, lipids and preventive cardiology
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 25, 27 (Primary Prevention, Lipoproteins)

mustKnow.fact: Atherogenesis begins with endothelial dysfunction, subendothelial accumulation and oxidation of apolipoprotein B-containing lipoproteins, and recruitment of monocyte-derived macrophages forming foam cells.
Familial hypercholesterolemia is predominantly caused by autosomal dominant mutations in the LDLR gene, followed by APOB and gain-of-function PCSK9 mutations.
Very high risk ASCVD guidelines recommend lowering LDL cholesterol by at least 50% from baseline and achieving an absolute LDL-C goal below 55 mg/dL.
Ezetimibe selectively inhibits the Niemann-Pick C1-Like 1 (NPC1L1) transporter in the jejunal brush border, reducing LDL-C by an additional 15% to 20% when added to statin therapy.
PCSK9 monoclonal antibodies evolocumab and alirocumab prevent degradation of LDL receptors, achieving further 50% to 60% LDL-C reductions.
Inclisiran is a small interfering RNA (siRNA) directed against PCSK9 mRNA in hepatocytes that produces sustained LDL-C lowering with biannual dosing.
Bempedoic acid inhibits adenosine triphosphate-citrate lyase (ACL) upstream of HMG-CoA reductase in the hepatic cholesterol synthesis pathway without causing muscular adverse effects.
Lipoprotein(a) is an independent genetically determined causal risk factor for ASCVD and calcific aortic stenosis when serum concentrations exceed 50 mg/dL or 125 nmol/L.

topics.title: Chronic coronary syndromes
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 40 (Stable Ischemic Heart Disease)

mustKnow.fact: Typical angina pectoris satisfies three criteria: substernal chest discomfort of characteristic quality and duration, provoked by exertion or emotional stress, and relieved by rest or sublingual nitroglycerin within minutes.

ISCHEMIA trial demonstrated that in patients with stable coronary disease and moderate-to-severe ischemia, an initial invasive strategy did not reduce the risk of ischemic cardiovascular events or death compared to optimal medical therapy.
First-line antianginal therapy consists of beta-blockers and/or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers to reduce myocardial oxygen consumption by blunting heart rate and contractility.

Ranolazine exerts antianginal effects by inhibiting late inward sodium current (late INa), reducing intracellular calcium overload and improving diastolic myocardial relaxation without affecting blood pressure or heart rate.
Nicorandil acts as a dual-mechanism antianginal through nitrate-like venodilation and ATP-sensitive potassium channel opening in coronary arterioles.

Ivabradine selectively inhibits the hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) funny current (If) in the sinoatrial node, reducing resting heart rate without affecting inotropy or blood pressure.

Ischemia with nonobstructive coronary arteries (INOCA) comprises coronary microvascular dysfunction and epicardial coronary vasospasm diagnosed invasively via coronary reactivity testing with acetylcholine.

Trimetazidine functions as a metabolic antianginal agent by selectively inhibiting mitochondrial 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase, shifting energy metabolism from fatty acid beta-oxidation toward more oxygen-efficient glucose oxidation.

topics.title: Non-ST elevation acute coronary syndromes
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 39 (Non-ST Elevation ACS)

mustKnow.fact: Fourth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction defines myocardial necrosis as a rise and/or fall of cardiac troponin with at least one value above the 99th percentile upper reference limit alongside clinical evidence of acute myocardial ischemia.
GRACE risk score evaluates in-hospital and 6-month mortality in ACS; a GRACE score above 140 identifies high-risk patients warranting early invasive coronary angiography within 24 hours.
TIMI risk score for NSTE-ACS incorporates 7 variables (age >= 65, >= 3 CAD risk factors, known CAD >= 50% stenosis, aspirin use, severe angina, elevated markers, ST deviation >= 0.5 mm).
High-sensitivity cardiac troponin 0/1-hour and 0/2-hour rapid rule-in and rule-out algorithms utilize baseline concentrations and absolute dynamic delta changes to safely triage NSTE-ACS.

Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) combining aspirin with a potent P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor or prasugrel) is recommended for 12 months following NSTE-ACS unless high bleeding risk warrants shortening.

Parenteral anticoagulation with low molecular weight heparin (enoxaparin) or unfractionated heparin is indicated during acute presentation, with fondaparinux preferred when an initial conservative strategy is chosen due to superior safety profile.

Very high risk NSTE-ACS criteria (hemodynamic instability, cardiogenic shock, recurrent refractory angina, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, mechanical complications) mandate immediate invasive coronary angiography within 2 hours.

MINOCA (myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries) requires diagnosis of acute MI, absence of obstructive CAD (stenosis < 50%), and exclusion of specific alternative causes such as myocarditis or takotsubo cardiomyopathy via CMR.

topics.title: ST elevation myocardial infarction
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 37, 38 (ST-Elevation MI: Pathophysiology and Management)

mustKnow.fact: Diagnostic ST-segment elevation requires new elevation at the J-point in two contiguous leads of >= 1 mm in all leads except V2-V3, where thresholds are >= 2.5 mm in men < 40, >= 2.0 mm in men >= 40, and >= 1.5 mm in women.
Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) is the preferred reperfusion strategy if it can be performed within 120 minutes of STEMI diagnosis.

If PPCI cannot be achieved within 120 minutes, intravenous fibrinolytic therapy (tenecteplase) must be administered within 10 minutes of STEMI diagnosis, followed by transfer for pharmacoinvasive angiography within 2 to 24 hours.
Posterior myocardial infarction is diagnosed by ST depression >= 0.5 mm in leads V1-V3 with tall R waves and upright T waves, confirmed by ST elevation >= 0.5 mm in posterior leads V7-V9.

Right ventricular infarction complicating inferior STEMI is identified by ST-segment elevation >= 1 mm in right-sided lead V4R, presenting with hypotension, clear lung fields, and elevated jugular venous pressure.

Modified Sgarbossa criteria identify acute coronary occlusion in the presence of left bundle branch block or ventricular pacing: concordant ST elevation >= 1 mm, concordant ST depression >= 1 mm in V1-V3, or excessively discordant ST/S ratio <= -0.25.
Prasugrel (60 mg loading dose, 10 mg daily maintenance) and ticagrelor (180 mg loading dose, 90 mg twice daily) are potent P2Y12 inhibitors preferred over clopidogrel in STEMI reperfusion.
Complete revascularization of non-infarct-related culprit arteries in hemodynamically stable STEMI multivessel disease reduces major adverse cardiac events as shown in the COMPLETE trial.

topics.title: Complications of myocardial infarction
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 38 (Mechanical, Electrical, and Hemodynamic Complications of MI)

mustKnow.fact: Mechanical rupture complications typically peak 3 to 5 days post-MI and include ventricular free wall rupture, ventricular septal rupture, and papillary muscle rupture causing acute mitral regurgitation.
Papillary muscle rupture most frequently involves the posteromedial papillary muscle because of its single blood supply from the posterior descending artery (RCA or LCx).
Ventricular septal rupture presents with a harsh holosystolic murmur with a thrill at the left sternal border and an oxygen saturation step-up >= 8% to 10% from right atrium to right ventricle.
Cardiogenic shock complicating acute MI is defined by systolic blood pressure < 90 mmHg, cardiac index < 2.2 L/min/m2, and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure > 15 mmHg accompanied by hypoperfusion.

Ventricular pseudoaneurysm results from a contained myocardial rupture bounded solely by pericardium, presenting with a narrow neck (neck-to-dome ratio < 0.5) and carrying a high risk of catastrophic rupture requiring emergent surgery.

Left ventricular true aneurysm consists of thinned, scarred, dyskinetic or akinetic myocardium with a wide neck (neck-to-dome ratio >= 0.9 to 1.0) rarely rupturing, but predisposing to mural thrombus and ventricular arrhythmias.

Dressler syndrome is a late autoimmune fibrinous pericarditis developing 2 to 10 weeks following myocardial infarction, characterized by fever, pleuropericardial pain, friction rub, and elevated inflammatory markers responsive to NSAIDs or colchicine.
Left ventricular mural thrombus occurs in up to 15% of anterior STEMIs, requiring oral anticoagulation with warfarin or a DOAC for at least 3 to 6 months.

topics.title: Percutaneous and surgical revascularisation
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 41 (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention and CABG)

mustKnow.fact: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) confers a survival advantage over PCI in patients with multivessel CAD and diabetes mellitus, high SYNTAX scores (> 32), or complex left main bifurcations.
The left internal mammary artery (LIMA) anastomosed to the left anterior descending (LAD) artery is the gold-standard bypass conduit with a 10-year patency rate exceeding 90%.

Radial artery bypass conduits demonstrate superior 5-year and 10-year patency compared to saphenous vein grafts, provided target coronary vessel stenosis is severe (>= 70% to 90%) to avoid competitive flow.

Second-generation drug-eluting stents (DES) eluting everolimus or zotarolimus with biocompatible or biodegradable polymers significantly reduce stent thrombosis and in-stent restenosis compared to bare-metal stents.

Stent thrombosis is classified by timing: acute (< 24 hours), subacute (24 hours to 30 days), late (30 days to 1 year), and very late (> 1 year), most often triggered by premature antiplatelet cessation or stent malapposition.
SYNTAX score stratifies CAD complexity based on coronary anatomy; low (0-22), intermediate (23-32), and high (>= 33) scores guide revascularization choice between PCI and CABG.
Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) uses acoustic shockwaves delivered via a balloon catheter to safely fracture superficial and deep circumferential vascular calcium prior to stent deployment.
Rotational atherectomy uses a diamond-coated burr rotating at 140,000 to 180,000 rpm to selectively ablate and debulk unyielding, heavily calcified coronary plaques.

modules.name: Heart failure pathophysiology and acute heart failure

topics.title: Heart failure pathophysiology and acute heart failure
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 48, 49 (Pathophysiology and Acute Heart Failure)

mustKnow.fact: Universal Definition of Heart Failure classifies patients based on ejection fraction into HFrEF (LVEF <= 40%), HFmrEF (LVEF 41% to 49%), and HFpEF (LVEF >= 50%).

Nohria-Stevenson clinical classification categorizes acute decompensated heart failure into four hemodynamic profiles: Warm-Dry (Profile A), Warm-Wet (Profile B), Cold-Wet (Profile C), and Cold-Dry (Profile L).

B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) cutoff < 100 pg/mL and NT-proBNP cutoff < 300 pg/mL have a negative predictive value > 95% for excluding acute decompensated heart failure in dyspneic emergency patients.
Intravenous loop diuretics (furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide) are initial therapy for congested acute heart failure, dosing 1 to 2.5 times the patient's chronic oral daily home dose.
Inotropic agents dobutamine (beta-1 adrenergic agonist) and milrinone (phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor) are reserved for acute cold-wet shock with hypoperfusion to restore end-organ perfusion.
Vasodilators such as intravenous nitroglycerin and sodium nitroprusside reduce preload and afterload in hypertensive acute pulmonary edema without worsening renal perfusion.
Cardiorenal syndrome type 1 involves acute kidney injury resulting directly from acute cardiac decompensation driven primarily by elevated central venous congestion rather than low cardiac output.

Levosimendan exerts inotropic and vasodilatory properties by calcium sensitization of cardiac troponin C and opening ATP-sensitive potassium channels in vascular smooth muscle without increasing myocardial oxygen consumption.

topics.title: Guideline-directed therapy for HFrEF
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 50 (Management of Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction)

mustKnow.fact: The four foundational pillars of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for HFrEF are ARNI/ACEi, evidence-based beta-blocker, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA), and SGLT2 inhibitor.

Sacubitril/valsartan (ARNI) reduces cardiovascular mortality and HF hospitalizations by 20% compared to enalapril in the PARADIGM-HF trial, requiring a mandatory 36-hour washout when switching from an ACE inhibitor to prevent angioedema.
Three evidence-based beta-blockers demonstrated to reduce mortality in HFrEF are carvedilol, metoprolol succinate extended-release, and bisoprolol.

Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists spironolactone and eplerenone reduce mortality in NYHA class II-IV HFrEF with LVEF <= 35%, requiring monitoring of serum potassium and eGFR (serum potassium <= 5.0 mEq/L, eGFR > 30 mL/min/1.73m2).
SGLT2 inhibitors dapagliflozin and empagliflozin significantly reduce cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalizations regardless of diabetes status in DAPA-HF and EMPEROR-Reduced trials.

Vericiguat, an oral soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC) stimulator, reduces cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization in worsening HFrEF patients recently hospitalized or receiving IV diuretics (VICTORIA trial).

Intravenous ferric carboxymaltose or ferric derisomaltose improves symptoms and reduces rehospitalizations in symptomatic HFrEF patients with iron deficiency defined as ferritin < 100 ng/mL or ferritin 100-299 ng/mL with TSAT < 20%.

Hydralazine combined with isosorbide dinitrate reduces mortality and improves exercise tolerance in self-identified Black patients with NYHA class III-IV HFrEF receiving optimal background therapy (A-HeFT trial).

modules.name: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

topics.title: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 51 (Heart Failure with Preserved and Mildly Reduced EF)

mustKnow.fact: HFpEF is characterized by symptoms and signs of heart failure with a normal or near-normal left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF >= 50%) and objective evidence of cardiac structural or functional abnormalities.

H2FPEF score uses 6 clinical variables (Heavy BMI > 30, Hypertensive >= 2 meds, Atrial Fibrillation, Pulmonary HTN PASP > 35, Elder age > 60, Filling pressure E/e > 9) to estimate probability of HFpEF.

HFA-PEFF diagnostic algorithm incorporates pretest assessment (Step 1), comprehensive echocardiographic and biomarker score (Step 2), functional testing via exercise stress echo or invasive hemodynamics (Step 3), and final etiology workup (Step 4).
Invasive exercise hemodynamics demonstrating pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) >= 15 mmHg at rest or >= 25 mmHg during exercise establishes the definitive diagnosis of HFpEF.

SGLT2 inhibitors (empagliflozin and dapagliflozin) are the first drug class proven to reduce composite cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization across the entire spectrum of HFpEF in EMPEROR-Preserved and DELIVER trials.
Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist spironolactone reduced heart failure hospitalizations in post-hoc regional analysis of the TOPCAT trial in patients with HFpEF from the Americas.
Sacubitril/valsartan showed greatest benefit in the PARAGON-HF trial among HFpEF subgroups with LVEF at the lower end of the preserved spectrum (LVEF < 57%) and in women.

Comorbidity management in HFpEF focuses on aggressive blood pressure control, rhythm or rate control of atrial fibrillation, weight loss, and screening for specific mimickers like cardiac amyloidosis.

modules.name: Device therapy, mechanical support and transplantation

topics.title: Device therapy, mechanical support and transplantation
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 58, 59, 60 (CRT, MCS, and Cardiac Transplantation)

mustKnow.fact: Cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) is indicated for symptomatic heart failure patients in sinus rhythm with LVEF <= 35%, QRS duration >= 150 ms, and left bundle branch block (LBBB) morphology.

Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) is indicated for primary prevention of sudden cardiac death in ischemic cardiomyopathy >= 40 days post-MI or nonischemic cardiomyopathy after >= 3 months of GDMT with LVEF <= 35% and NYHA class II-III.

Subcutaneous ICD (S-ICD) avoids transvenous lead complications, recommended for ICD candidates without pacing indication for bradycardia, CRT requirement, or recurrent monomorphic VT amenable to antitachycardia pacing.

Intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) provides counterpulsation by inflating in early diastole at the dicrotic notch to augment coronary perfusion and deflating immediately before systole to reduce afterload.

Impella percutaneous microaxial continuous-flow pump aspirates blood directly from the left ventricle across the aortic valve and expels it into the ascending aorta, delivering up to 2.5 to 5.5 L/min of forward flow.

Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) provides biventricular circulatory and gas exchange support, but increases left ventricular afterload, often requiring active LV venting via IABP or Impella (ECPELLA).

Durable continuous-flow left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) like HeartMate 3 utilize full magnetically levitated centrifugal rotors to prevent hemocompatibility-related adverse events such as pump thrombosis.

Orthotopic cardiac transplantation is the gold-standard definitive therapy for refractory end-stage heart failure, yielding a median post-transplant survival of approximately 12 to 14 years with maintenance calcineurin-inhibitor immunosuppression.

topics.title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 54 (Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy)

mustKnow.fact: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is an autosomal dominant disease of the cardiac sarcomere, most commonly caused by mutations in MYBPC3 and MYH7 encoding cardiac myosin-binding protein C and beta-myosin heavy chain.

Echocardiographic diagnostic criterion for HCM in adults without family history is unexplained left ventricular wall thickness >= 15 mm in one or more myocardial segments (or >= 13 mm in first-degree relatives of affected patients).

Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction is defined by a peak resting or provocable gradient >= 30 mmHg, with severe obstruction defined at >= 50 mmHg driven by systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve.

Mavacamten is a first-in-class cardiac myosin ATPase inhibitor that reduces actin-myosin cross-bridge formation, relieving LVOT gradients and improving NYHA functional class in symptomatic obstructive HCM (EXPLORER-HCM).
Surgical septal myectomy (Morrow procedure) is the gold-standard septal reduction therapy for drug-refractory obstructive HCM with peak gradient >= 50 mmHg.
Alcohol septal ablation achieves septal reduction via catheter-mediated percutaneous infarction of the target septal perforator branch guided by myocardial contrast echocardiography.

Major risk markers for sudden cardiac death in HCM include massive hypertrophy (wall thickness >= 30 mm), unexplained recent syncope, family history of SCD, LV apical aneurysm, and extensive LGE >= 15% of LV mass.

Apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (Yamaguchi syndrome) exhibits giant inverted T waves in precordial leads V2-V6 and an ace-of-spades spade-like configuration of the left ventricular cavity during end-diastole on ventriculography.

topics.title: Dilated, restrictive and arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 52, 55 (Dilated and Restrictive Cardiomyopathies, ARVC)

mustKnow.fact: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is characterized by left ventricular enlargement and systolic dysfunction (LVEF < 45% or fractional shortening < 25%) in the absence of abnormal loading conditions or ischemic disease.
TTN gene truncating variants (titin-truncating variants or TTNtvs) represent the most prevalent genetic cause of familial dilated cardiomyopathy, accounting for up to 15% to 25% of inherited cases.

LMNA mutations encoding nuclear envelope lamins A/C cause DCM characterized by high penetrance of early progressive AV block, atrial arrhythmias, and high malignant ventricular tachycardia risk warranting early primary ICD placement.
Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) is caused by mutations in desmosomal genes (PKP2, DSP, DSG2, DSC2, JUP) leading to fibrofatty replacement of right ventricular myocardium.
Diagnostic hallmarks of ARVC on 12-lead ECG include epsilon waves (small positive deflections at the end of QRS) in leads V1-V3 and inverted T waves in right precordial leads beyond age 14.

Restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM) is characterized by rigid ventricular walls resulting in severe diastolic dysfunction with restrictive filling pattern (mitral E/A ratio > 2.0, deceleration time < 160 ms), normal or near-normal wall thickness, and biatrial enlargement.

Differentiation between constrictive pericarditis and restrictive cardiomyopathy relies on invasive hemodynamics demonstrating ventricular interdependence (discordant RV-LV systolic pressures during respiration) in constriction but not in restriction.
Naxos disease is an autosomal recessive cardiocutaneous syndrome combining ARVC with woolly hair and palmoplantar keratoderma caused by homozygous mutations in plakoglobin (JUP).

topics.title: Myocarditis and inflammatory cardiomyopathy
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 56 (Myocarditis)

mustKnow.fact: Dallas criteria define active myocarditis on endomyocardial biopsy as an inflammatory infiltrate of the myocardium associated with myocyte degeneration or necrosis of non-ischemic origin.

Updated Lake Louise Criteria for cardiac MRI diagnosis of myocarditis require at least one T1-based criterion (increased myocardial T1 relaxation time, extracellular volume, or late gadolinium enhancement) and one T2-based criterion (increased T2 relaxation time or T2 signal intensity ratio).

Fulminant myocarditis presents with abrupt cardiogenic shock and refractory ventricular arrhythmias following a viral prodrome, requiring rapid temporary mechanical circulatory support (VA-ECMO or Impella) with excellent long-term survival in responders.

Giant cell myocarditis is an aggressive autoimmune myocarditis characterized by multinucleated giant cells and diffuse myocardial necrosis, carrying high mortality unless treated with aggressive immunosuppression (cyclosporine, corticosteroids) or emergent transplantation.

Cardiac sarcoidosis manifests with high-grade AV block, ventricular arrhythmias, or heart failure, diagnosed via cardiac 18F-FDG PET demonstrating patchy focal myocardial hypermetabolism matching late gadolinium enhancement.

Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI myocarditis) occurs within 1 to 3 months of PD-1/CTLA-4 inhibitor initiation, often presenting with concurrent myositis or myasthenia gravis and treated promptly with high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone (1000 mg daily).

Eosinophilic myocarditis (hypereosinophilic syndrome or Loeffler endocarditis) progresses from an initial acute necrotic phase to a thrombotic phase with extensive endocardial mural thrombi and late restrictive fibroelastosis.

Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (stress-induced cardiomyopathy) is characterized by transient apical and midventricular ballooning mimicking acute STEMI without obstructive CAD, triggered by catecholamine surge and managed with supportive care.

topics.title: Cardiac amyloidosis and infiltrative disease
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 53 (Cardiac Amyloidosis and Infiltrative Disease)

mustKnow.fact: Cardiac amyloidosis is caused primarily by myocardial extracellular deposition of misfolded light chain fibrils (AL amyloidosis) or transthyretin fibrils (ATTR amyloidosis, wild-type or hereditary).
Classic ECG-echocardiography discordance in cardiac amyloidosis consists of low limb lead QRS voltage (< 5 mm) despite striking concentric biventricular pseudohypertrophy on imaging.
Apical sparing pattern on speckle-tracking echocardiography strain analysis (cherry on top appearance) has high diagnostic sensitivity and specificity for cardiac amyloidosis.

Non-biopsy diagnostic criteria for ATTR cardiac amyloidosis require Grade 2 or 3 myocardial uptake on 99mTc-PYP or DPD bone scintigraphy along with completely negative serum free light chain assay and immunofixation electrophoresis.

Tafamidis is a selective transthyretin tetramer stabilizer that binds the thyroxine-binding sites, reducing all-cause mortality and cardiovascular hospitalizations in wild-type and hereditary ATTR cardiomyopathy (ATTR-ACT trial).
ATTR gene silencers patisiran and vutrisiran (siRNAs) or inotersen and eplontersen (antisense oligonucleotides) suppress hepatic TTR protein synthesis by targeting TTR messenger RNA.

AL cardiac amyloidosis requires urgent clone-directed systemic chemotherapy combining daratumumab, bortezomib, cyclophosphamide, and dexamethasone (Dara-VCD) followed by autologous stem cell transplantation in eligible patients.

Fabry disease is an X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-galactosidase A deficiency leading to globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) accumulation, presenting with concentric LVH, short PR interval, and inferolateral midwall LGE on CMR.

modules.name: Rheumatic heart disease and mitral valve disease

topics.title: Rheumatic heart disease and mitral valve disease
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 74, 75, 81 (Mitral Stenosis, Mitral Regurgitation, Rheumatic Fever)

mustKnow.fact: Severe mitral stenosis is hemodynamically defined by a mitral valve area (MVA) <= 1.5 cm2 (very severe <= 1.0 cm2) and transmitral pressure half-time >= 150 ms (very severe >= 220 ms).

Wilkins echocardiographic score assesses mitral valve leaflet mobility, subvalvular thickening, leaflet thickening, and calcification (scale 1 to 4 each, maximum 16), where a score <= 8 predicts successful percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy (PMBC).

Contraindications to PMBC in rheumatic mitral stenosis include left atrial thrombus, more than mild mitral regurgitation (grade > 2+), severe bicommissural calcification, or concomitant severe aortic valve disease.
Primary (degenerative) mitral regurgitation is defined as severe when effective regurgitant orifice area (EROA) is >= 0.40 cm2 and regurgitant volume is >= 60 mL.
Class I surgical indication for asymptomatic severe primary MR requires left ventricular systolic dysfunction defined by LVEF <= 60% or left ventricular end-systolic diameter (LVESD) >= 40 mm.

Secondary (functional) mitral regurgitation results from LV remodeling causing papillary muscle displacement and leaflet tethering, with severe MR defined by EROA >= 0.20 cm2 and regurgitant volume >= 30 mL.

Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) using MitraClip improves survival and reduces HF hospitalizations in secondary MR matching the COAPT trial criteria (LVEF 20%-50%, LVESD <= 70 mm, persistent symptoms on maximal GDMT).

Revised Jones Criteria for acute rheumatic fever require evidence of preceding group A streptococcal infection plus two major criteria (carditis, polyarthritis, chorea, erythema marginatum, subcutaneous nodules) or one major plus two minor criteria.

topics.title: Aortic valve disease
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 72, 73 (Aortic Stenosis and Aortic Regurgitation)

mustKnow.fact: Severe high-gradient aortic stenosis is defined by peak aortic jet velocity >= 4.0 m/s, mean transaortic pressure gradient >= 40 mmHg, and aortic valve area <= 1.0 cm2 (or indexed AVA <= 0.6 cm2/m2).

Classical low-flow, low-gradient severe AS features AVA <= 1.0 cm2 with mean gradient < 40 mmHg and reduced LVEF (< 50%), requiring low-dose dobutamine stress echocardiography to differentiate true-severe AS from pseudo-severe AS by assessing contractile reserve.

Paradoxical low-flow, low-gradient severe AS features AVA <= 1.0 cm2 with mean gradient < 40 mmHg despite preserved LVEF (>= 50%), characterized by severe concentric LV remodeling with low stroke volume index (< 35 mL/m2) confirmed by noncontrast cardiac CT calcium scoring.

Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is preferred over surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in patients aged >= 75 to 80 years or those at high/prohibitive surgical risk, with transfemoral access being the standard route.

Bicuspid aortic valve is the most common congenital cardiac malformation (prevalence 1% to 2%), characterized by Sievers classification (Types 0, 1, and 2 based on raphe presence) and strongly associated with ascending aortic aneurysm and coarctation.

Severe chronic aortic regurgitation is defined by Doppler jet width >= 65% of LVOT, vena contracta width > 6 mm, pressure half-time < 200 ms, holodiastolic flow reversal in descending aorta, and regurgitant volume >= 60 mL.
Class I surgical triggers for asymptomatic severe aortic regurgitation include resting LVEF <= 50% or severe LV dilation with LV end-systolic dimension (LVESD) > 50 mm (or indexed LVESD > 25 mm/m2).

Peripheral vascular signs of severe chronic aortic regurgitation result from wide pulse pressure: Corrigan water-hammer pulse, de Musset sign (head nodding), Quincke pulse (capillary pulsation), Traube sign (pistol-shot sound), and Duroziez sign (to-and-fro femoral murmur).

topics.title: Tricuspid, pulmonary and prosthetic valves
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 77, 79 (Tricuspid/Pulmonic Valve Disease, Prosthetic Heart Valves)

mustKnow.fact: Secondary (functional) tricuspid regurgitation accounts for > 90% of cases, driven by tricuspid annular dilation (diastolic diameter >= 40 mm or > 21 mm/m2) and RV remodeling secondary to left-sided heart disease or pulmonary hypertension.

Severe tricuspid regurgitation features vena contracta width >= 7 mm, hepatic vein systolic flow reversal, dense triangular early-peaking continuous wave Doppler jet, and effective regurgitant orifice area >= 0.40 cm2.

Ebstein anomaly is characterized by apical displacement of the septal and posterior tricuspid valve leaflets >= 8 mm/m2 from the anterior mitral annulus, creating an atrialized portion of the right ventricle.

Mechanical prosthetic valves require lifelong oral anticoagulation with vitamin K antagonists (warfarin), targeting an INR of 2.5 for bileaflet aortic valves without risk factors, and INR of 3.0 for mechanical mitral valves or aortic valves with thromboembolic risk factors.
Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are strictly contraindicated in patients with mechanical heart valves based on the RE-ALIGN trial showing excess thromboembolism and bleeding with dabigatran.

Prosthetic valve thrombosis presents with new murmur, dyspnea, or elevated transvalvular Doppler gradients, managed with slow-infusion low-dose tissue plasminogen activator (tPA 25 mg over 25 hours) for obstructive thrombosis when surgical risk is prohibitive.

Structural valve deterioration of bioprosthetic valves occurs via leaflet calcification, tearing, or fibrosis, typically emerging 10 to 15 years post-implantation and treatable via transcatheter valve-in-valve (ViV) procedures.

Paravalvular regurgitation (paravalvular leak) results from incomplete annular sealing or infection, causing hemolytic anemia with elevated LDH and schistocytes or heart failure, amenable to percutaneous transcatheter plug closure.

topics.title: Infective endocarditis
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 80 (Infective Endocarditis)

mustKnow.fact: Modified Duke Criteria diagnose infective endocarditis using major criteria (persistently positive blood cultures for typical organisms, imaging evidence of endocardial involvement) and minor criteria (predisposition, fever >= 38 C, vascular phenomena, immunologic phenomena, microbiologic evidence).

Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) has a superior diagnostic sensitivity of 90% to 100% compared to transthoracic echo (TTE 60% to 75%) for detecting vegetations, perivalvular abscesses, and prosthetic valve endocarditis.
Staphylococcus aureus is the leading etiologic organism of native valve endocarditis worldwide, associated with acute destructive course, high embolic risk, and neurological complications.
Streptococcus gallolyticus (formerly S. bovis) endocarditis strongly correlates with occult colorectal neoplasms, necessitating mandatory full colonoscopy during hospitalization.
Culture-negative endocarditis accounts for 5% to 10% of cases, commonly caused by fastidious organisms: Coxiella burnetii (Q fever), Bartonella species, Tropheryma whipplei, and the HACEK group.

Class I indications for urgent early surgery in infective endocarditis are heart failure refractory to medical therapy, uncontrolled local infection (abscess, fistula, enlarging vegetation), and persistent large mobile vegetations (> 10 mm) following embolic episodes.

Antibiotic prophylaxis before invasive dental procedures involving gingival manipulation is indicated exclusively for high-risk patients: prosthetic valves, prosthetic material for valve repair, previous endocarditis, and unrepaired cyanotic congenital heart disease.

Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (marantic endocarditis) features sterile platelet-fibrin vegetations along valve coaptation lines associated with advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas or antiphospholipid syndrome.

topics.title: Atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 66 (Atrial Fibrillation and Flutter)

mustKnow.fact: CHA2DS2-VASc score stratifies stroke risk in nonvalvular AF, where oral anticoagulation is recommended (Class I) for men with score >= 2 and women with score >= 3.

Direct oral anticoagulants (apixaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, rivaroxaban) are preferred over warfarin for nonvalvular AF due to lower intracranial hemorrhage rates and noninferior or superior stroke prevention.

Catheter ablation via pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using radiofrequency or cryoballoon is superior to antiarrhythmic drugs for maintaining sinus rhythm and improving symptoms in paroxysmal and persistent AF (EAST-AFNET 4).

Pulsed field ablation (PFA) delivers non-thermal irreversible electroporation that selectively destabilizes cardiomyocyte cell membranes while sparing adjacent esophagus, phrenic nerve, and coronary vessels.

Typical atrial flutter is macro-reentrant around the tricuspid annulus dependent on the cavotricuspid isthmus (CTI), exhibiting negative sawtooth flutter waves in inferior leads II, III, aVF and curable with CTI catheter ablation.
Rate control targets a resting heart rate < 110 bpm (lenient rate control from RACE II trial) using beta-blockers, non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (diltiazem, verapamil), or digoxin.
Left atrial appendage occlusion (Watchman, Amulet) provides mechanical stroke prophylaxis in patients with high thromboembolic risk and absolute lifelong contraindications to oral anticoagulation.

Cardioversion of AF of >= 48 hours duration or unknown onset mandates either continuous therapeutic anticoagulation for >= 3 weeks prior and >= 4 weeks post-procedure, or immediate transesophageal echocardiography to rule out left atrial appendage thrombus.

topics.title: Supraventricular tachycardias and preexcitation
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 65 (Supraventricular Tachycardias)

mustKnow.fact: Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT) utilizes dual AV nodal pathways (slow pathway with short refractory period and fast pathway with long refractory period), presenting with pseudo-r' in V1 and pseudo-S in inferior leads.
Catheter ablation of the slow pathway in the inferior triangle of Koch achieves a cure rate > 95% for typical slow-fast AVNRT with low risk (< 1%) of complete AV block.

Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome features preexcitation with short PR interval (< 120 ms), slurred delta wave upstroke, and wide QRS complex (> 120 ms) due to an accessory atrioventricular bypass tract (Bundle of Kent).

Pre-excited atrial fibrillation in WPW conducts rapidly down the accessory pathway causing an irregularly irregular wide-complex tachycardia that may degenerate into ventricular fibrillation; AV nodal blockers (adenosine, verapamil, diltiazem, digoxin, beta-blockers) are strictly contraindicated.

Acute management of pre-excited AF in WPW requires electrical cardioversion if hemodynamically unstable, or intravenous procainamide or ibutilide if stable to prolong accessory pathway refractory period.

Orthodromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT) conducts antegrade down the AV node and retrograde up the accessory pathway, producing a narrow-complex tachycardia responsive to vagal maneuvers or IV adenosine.
Antidromic AVRT conducts antegrade down the accessory pathway and retrograde up the AV node, resulting in a wide-complex regular tachycardia resembling ventricular tachycardia.
Focal atrial tachycardia arises from localized atrial foci (crista terminalis, pulmonary veins, coronary sinus ostium), demonstrating centrifugal P wave spread and warm-up/cool-down rate variations.

modules.name: Ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death

topics.title: Ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 67, 70 (Ventricular Arrhythmias and Cardiac Arrest)

mustKnow.fact: Brugada criteria for differentiating ventricular tachycardia (VT) from supraventricular tachycardia with aberrancy examine 4 sequential steps: absence of RS complex in all precordial leads, RS interval > 100 ms, AV dissociation, and classic morphology criteria.

Vereckei aVR algorithm diagnoses VT if lead aVR shows initial R wave, initial r or q wave width > 40 ms, notch on descending limb of negative QRS, or ventricular-to-atrial activation velocity ratio (Vi/Vt) <= 1.

Idiopathic right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) VT is a benign adenosine-sensitive cAMP-mediated triggered arrhythmia showing left bundle branch block morphology with an inferior axis (tall positive R waves in leads II, III, aVF).

Idiopathic left ventricular fascicular VT (Belhassen VT) originates from the posterior fascicle, presenting with RBBB morphology and superior left axis deviation, uniquely responsive to intravenous verapamil.

Scar-related monomorphic VT in ischemic cardiomyopathy is driven by reentry around myocardial infarct border-zone channels, amenable to substrate-based catheter ablation targeting fractionated late potentials.

Electrical storm is defined by >= 3 separate episodes of sustained VT/VF within a 24-hour period, managed by deep sedation, beta-blockade, intravenous amiodarone, sympathetic blockade (stellate ganglion block), and catheter ablation.

Torsades de pointes is a polymorphic VT occurring in the setting of prolonged QT interval, displaying characteristic twisting of QRS complexes around the isoelectric line, treated acutely with intravenous magnesium sulfate (2 g bolus) and overdrive pacing.
Secondary prevention ICD implantation reduces mortality in survivors of cardiac arrest due to VF or hemodynamically unstable sustained VT not due to a completely reversible cause.

topics.title: Bradyarrhythmias, conduction disease and pacing
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 68, 69 (Bradyarrhythmias, AV Block, and Pacemakers)

mustKnow.fact: Sick sinus syndrome (sinus node dysfunction) encompasses sinus bradycardia, sinus arrest, sinoatrial exit block, and tachycardia-bradycardia syndrome, where symptomatic chronotropic incompetence is a primary indication for permanent pacing.
Second-degree Mobitz type I (Wenckebach) AV block features progressive PR prolongation before a nonconducted P wave, localized to the AV node and generally benign.

Second-degree Mobitz type II AV block features constant PR intervals prior to sudden dropped P waves, located in the infranodal His-Purkinje system with high risk of progression to complete heart block, warranting Class I pacemaker indication.
Third-degree (complete) AV block demonstrates complete atrioventricular dissociation where atrial rate exceeds ventricular rate, requiring permanent pacemaker implantation.

Conduction system pacing (His bundle pacing and left bundle branch area pacing) captures native specialized conduction tissue directly, preventing pacing-induced LV dyssynchrony caused by traditional RV apical pacing.
Pacemaker syndrome occurs in single-chamber ventricular pacing (VVI mode) due to loss of AV synchrony and retrograde ventriculoatrial conduction causing cannon A waves and hypotension.
Leadless pacemakers (Micra, Aveir) are self-contained intracardiac capsules deployed transcatheterly into the right ventricle, eliminating pocket infections, lead fractures, and vascular occlusions.

Trifascicular block on ECG is defined by complete RBBB with left anterior or posterior fascicular block and alternating bundle branch block or first-degree AV block, carrying a high risk of sudden progression to complete AV block.

topics.title: Inherited arrhythmia syndromes
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 63 (Genetics of Cardiac Arrhythmias and Channelopathies)

mustKnow.fact: Congenital Long QT Syndrome type 1 (LQT1, KCNQ1 mutation) is triggered by exercise or swimming, type 2 (LQT2, KCNH2) by auditory stimuli or emotional stress, and type 3 (LQT3, SCN5A) during sleep or rest.
Schwartz score >= 3.5 establishes high diagnostic probability of congenital LQTS based on QTc duration, T-wave alternans, notched T waves, syncope history, and family history.

Brugada syndrome is an autosomal dominant channelopathy caused by loss-of-function mutations in SCN5A (voltage-gated sodium channel subunit alpha), unmasked by sodium channel blockers (ajmaline, flecainide).
Quinidine, a class Ia antiarrhythmic with Ito blocking properties, is effective pharmacotherapy for suppressing recurrent ventricular fibrillation storms in Brugada syndrome and short QT syndrome.

Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT) is caused by mutations in RYR2 (ryanodine receptor 2) or CASQ2, presenting with exercise- or emotion-induced bidirectional ventricular tachycardia in young patients with normal resting ECG.
Flecainide combined with beta-blockers provides potent antiarrhythmic suppression in CPVT by directly inhibiting RyR2-mediated sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release and blocking peak sodium current.
Short QT syndrome is defined by QTc <= 340 ms (or QTc < 360 ms with symptoms/family history) caused by gain-of-function mutations in potassium channel genes (KCNH2, KCNQ1, KCNJ2).

Early repolarization syndrome is diagnosed by J-point elevation >= 1 mm in >= 2 contiguous inferior and/or lateral leads with notched or slurred J waves in survivors of unexplained cardiac arrest or polymorphic VT/VF.

topics.title: Antiarrhythmic drugs
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 64 (Therapy for Cardiac Arrhythmias)

mustKnow.fact: Vaughan Williams classification categorizes antiarrhythmics into Class I (sodium channel blockers: Ia quinidine/procainamide, Ib lidocaine/mexiletine, Ic flecainide/propafenone), Class II (beta-blockers), Class III (potassium channel blockers: amiodarone/sotalol/dofetilide), and Class IV (calcium channel blockers: verapamil/diltiazem).

CAST trial demonstrated that Class Ic antiarrhythmics (flecainide, encainide) significantly increase mortality in patients with structural heart disease or prior myocardial infarction due to proarrhythmic sodium channel blockade.

Amiodarone exhibits electrophysiologic properties of all four Vaughan Williams classes, safe in HFrEF, but associated with multi-organ toxicities: pulmonary fibrosis, thyroid dysfunction (hypo- and hyperthyroidism), corneal microdeposits, hepatotoxicity, and blue-gray skin discoloration.

Dronedarone is a non-iodinated amiodarone analogue lacking thyroid and pulmonary toxicity, but strictly contraindicated in decompensated heart failure or permanent AF due to increased mortality in ANDROMEDA and PALLAS trials.

Sotalol is a nonselective beta-blocker with Class III rapid delayed rectifier potassium current (IKr) blocking activity exhibiting reverse use-dependence, requiring inpatient telemetry initiation and QTc monitoring to prevent torsades de pointes.
Dofetilide is a pure selective IKr blocker requiring strict in-hospital renal dose titration and serial QTc monitoring, safe in patients with heart failure or reduced LVEF.

Adenosine activates A1 adenosine receptors in the AV node causing G protein-mediated opening of inward rectifier potassium channels (IKAch) and hyperpolarization, abruptly terminating AV nodal-dependent reentrant tachycardias with a half-life < 10 seconds.

Ibutilide is an intravenous Class III agent that promotes slow inward sodium current while blocking delayed rectifier potassium channels, highly effective for acute pharmacological termination of recent-onset atrial flutter and fibrillation.

topics.title: Syncope
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 71 (Syncope and Autonomic Disorders)

mustKnow.fact: Syncope is defined as a transient loss of consciousness due to global cerebral hypoperfusion, characterized by rapid onset, short duration, and spontaneous complete recovery.

Reflex (neurally mediated) syncope includes vasovagal syncope, situational syncope, and carotid sinus syndrome, mediated by inappropriate cardioinhibition (bradycardia/asystole) and/or vasodepression (hypotension).

Carotid sinus massage is positive for carotid sinus hypersensitivity when producing ventricular asystole >= 3 seconds (cardioinhibitory) or a fall in systolic blood pressure >= 50 mmHg (vasodepressor).
Orthostatic hypotension is diagnosed by a sustained reduction in systolic blood pressure >= 20 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure >= 10 mmHg within 3 minutes of standing or head-up tilt testing.

Cardiac syncope caused by structural heart disease or primary electrical arrhythmias carries the highest risk of sudden cardiac death, flagged by syncope during exertion, in the supine position, preceded by palpitations, or without prodrome.

Implantable loop recorders (ILRs) provide continuous subcutaneous ECG monitoring for up to 3 to 4 years, representing the highest diagnostic yield test for recurrent unexplained syncope of suspected arrhythmic origin.

Electrophysiology study (EPS) in syncope evaluation is indicated in patients with previous MI or structural heart disease where non-invasive testing is non-diagnostic, assessing HV interval (abnormal if >= 70 ms) and VT inducibility.

Midodrine (alpha-1 agonist) and fludrocortisone (mineralocorticoid volume expander) are first-line pharmacotherapies for refractory neurogenic orthostatic hypotension and severe vasodepressor reflex syncope.

topics.title: Pericardial disease
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 86 (Pericardial Diseases)

mustKnow.fact: Acute pericarditis requires at least two of four diagnostic criteria: pleuritic chest pain improved by sitting forward, pericardial friction rub, widespread concave ST-segment elevation with PR depression, and new or worsening pericardial effusion.

First-line therapy for acute idiopathic or viral pericarditis consists of high-dose NSAIDs (aspirin 750-1000 mg or ibuprofen 600 mg every 8 hours) plus weight-adjusted colchicine (0.5 mg once or twice daily) for 3 months to prevent recurrences.
Beck triad of cardiac tamponade comprises systemic hypotension, muffled or distant heart sounds, and elevated jugular venous pressure with prominent x descent and absent y descent.
Pulsus paradoxus is defined as an inspiratory decline in systolic blood pressure > 10 mmHg during normal quiet breathing, resulting from exaggerated ventricular interdependence in cardiac tamponade.

Echocardiographic signs of tamponade include right ventricular diastolic collapse, right atrial late diastolic collapse lasting > one-third of the cardiac cycle, and > 25% respiratory variation in mitral inflow E velocity.

Constrictive pericarditis features dense fibrocalcific pericardial scarring leading to elevated equalized diastolic filling pressures, prominent early rapid ventricular filling followed by sudden cessation creating the square root or dip-and-plateau pressure tracing.

Kussmaul sign is an abnormal paradoxical rise or lack of normal inspiratory fall in jugular venous pressure during inspiration, commonly observed in constrictive pericarditis, RV infarction, and restrictive cardiomyopathy.

Anakinra, an interleukin-1 (IL-1) receptor antagonist, is highly effective for corticosteroid-dependent, colchicine-resistant recurrent pericarditis by targeting autoinflammatory inflammasome activation (AIRTRIP trial).

topics.title: Systemic hypertension
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 26 (Systemic Hypertension)

mustKnow.fact: Primary aldosteronism (Conn syndrome) is the most common secondary cause of hypertension (accounting for 5% to 10% of cases), screened by plasma aldosterone-to-renin ratio (ARR > 20 to 30) and confirmed by salt loading or fludrocortisone suppression testing.

Renal artery stenosis due to atherosclerotic disease or fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) leads to renovascular hypertension, where FMD demonstrates classic string-of-beads appearance on angiography in young females.

Hypertensive emergency is defined as severe blood pressure elevation (> 180/120 mmHg) associated with acute hypertension-mediated organ damage (HMOD), requiring intravenous labetalol, nicardipine, or nitroprusside.

Target blood pressure lowering in hypertensive emergency (except aortic dissection, acute ischemic stroke, or pheochromocytoma) is a cautious reduction of MAP by no more than 20% to 25% within the first hour to prevent ischemic hypoperfusion.

Resistant hypertension is defined as blood pressure remaining above target despite concurrent use of three antihypertensive agents of different classes (including a diuretic, RAAS blocker, and CCB) at maximal tolerated doses.

Spironolactone (25 to 50 mg daily) is the preferred fourth-line agent for resistant hypertension, effectively countering unrecognized mineralocorticoid excess and sodium retention as shown in PATHWAY-2.

Catheter-based renal sympathetic denervation utilizes radiofrequency energy or targeted ultrasound to ablate renal efferent and afferent nerves in main and branch renal arteries, reducing blood pressure in resistant hypertension.
Pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma secrete catecholamines producing paroxysmal hypertension, headaches, sweating, and tachycardia, diagnosed by 24-hour urinary or plasma fractionated metanephrines.

topics.title: Diseases of the aorta
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 42 (Diseases of the Aorta)

mustKnow.fact: Stanford classification divides acute aortic dissection into Type A (involving ascending aorta regardless of tear site) requiring emergent surgical repair, and Type B (limited to descending aorta distal to left subclavian artery) managed medically unless complicated.

Initial medical management of acute aortic dissection targets heart rate < 60 bpm and systolic blood pressure between 100 and 120 mmHg using intravenous beta-blockers (esmolol, labetalol) to decrease aortic wall shear stress (dP/dt).

Intramural hematoma (IMH) is an acute aortic syndrome resulting from rupture of aortic wall vasa vasorum without an intimal flap or false lumen flow, carrying similar catastrophic rupture risk as overt dissection.

Penetrating atherosclerotic ulcer (PAU) describes deep erosion of an atheromatous plaque through the internal elastic lamina into the aortic media, typically occurring in elderly hypertensive smokers.

Thoracic aortic aneurysm surgical threshold for asymptomatic ascending aorta is >= 5.5 cm in degenerative aneurysm (or >= 5.0 cm in bicuspid aortic valve with risk factors, and >= 4.5 cm in Marfan syndrome with risk factors).

Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) repair is indicated when maximum transverse diameter reaches >= 5.5 cm in men or >= 5.0 cm in women, or with rapid expansion exceeding 0.5 cm in 6 months or 1.0 cm in 1 year.

Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) is the preferred intervention for complicated acute Type B dissection (refractory pain, malperfusion syndrome, rapid expansion, or rupture) to cover the primary entry tear and promote false lumen thrombosis.

Aortitis and large-vessel vasculitis predominantly comprise Takayasu arteritis (affecting young women < 40 years, pulseless disease) and Giant cell arteritis (affecting adults > 50 years, temporal arteritis).

topics.title: Pulmonary hypertension
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 88 (Pulmonary Hypertension)

mustKnow.fact: Pulmonary hypertension is hemodynamically defined by a resting mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) > 20 mmHg measured by right heart catheterization.

Pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension (Group 1 PAH, Group 3 lung disease, Group 4 CTEPH) requires mPAP > 20 mmHg, pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) <= 15 mmHg, and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) > 2 Wood units.

Post-capillary pulmonary hypertension (Group 2 left heart disease) requires mPAP > 20 mmHg and PCWP > 15 mmHg, subdivided into isolated post-capillary (IpcPH, PVR <= 2 Wood units) and combined post- and pre-capillary (CpcPH, PVR > 2 Wood units).
Endothelin receptor antagonists (bosentan, ambrisentan, macitentan) block ET-1 mediated vasoconstriction and vascular remodeling in pulmonary arterial hypertension.

Phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE-5) inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil) and soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator riociguat augment nitric oxide-cGMP signaling, with co-administration of PDE-5 inhibitors and riociguat strictly contraindicated due to severe systemic hypotension.

Prostacyclin pathway agonists (epoprostenol, treprostinil, iloprost, selexipag) induce direct pulmonary vasodilation and inhibit platelet aggregation, with continuous intravenous epoprostenol proven to improve survival in high-risk NYHA class IV PAH.

Sotatercept is a first-in-class activin signaling inhibitor (activin receptor type IIA-Fc fusion protein) that restores balance between pro-proliferative activin and anti-proliferative BMPR2 signaling pathways in PAH (STELLAR trial).

Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH, Group 4) is diagnosed via ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) scan demonstrating mismatched segmental perfusion defects, with pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) being the potential curative treatment of choice.

modules.name: Pulmonary embolism and peripheral arterial disease

topics.title: Pulmonary embolism and peripheral arterial disease
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 43, 87 (Peripheral Artery Disease, Pulmonary Embolism)

mustKnow.fact: High-risk (massive) pulmonary embolism is defined by hemodynamic instability (sustained hypotension SBP < 90 mmHg, vasopressor requirement, or cardiac arrest), mandating immediate systemic thrombolytic therapy with recombinant tPA (100 mg over 2 hours).

Intermediate-high risk (submassive) PE features both right ventricular dysfunction on imaging (echo RV dilation or CT RV/LV ratio >= 1.0) and elevated cardiac biomarkers (positive troponin or NT-proBNP) in hemodynamically stable patients.

PESI (Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index) and simplified PESI (sPESI) calculate 30-day all-cause mortality, where an sPESI score of 0 identifies low-risk PE patients suitable for early hospital discharge or home management.

Catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) and percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy provide effective clot removal with reduced bleeding risk in intermediate-high risk PE patients exhibiting clinical deterioration.

Ankle-brachial index (ABI) is the primary non-invasive diagnostic test for peripheral artery disease, where a resting ABI <= 0.90 is diagnostic of PAD, and ABI > 1.40 indicates noncompressible calcified vessels (Mönckeberg sclerosis).

Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI, Rutherford categories 4-6, Fontaine stages III-IV) manifests as ischemic rest pain, nonhealing ischemic ulcers, or gangrene requiring urgent revascularization to prevent amputation.

WIfI classification stratifies amputation risk and revascularization benefit in CLTI by scoring Wound extent (W), Ischemia severity via toe pressure or ABI (I), and Foot Infection (fI) from grades 0 to 3 each.

Cilostazol is a phosphodiesterase-3 (PDE-3) inhibitor with vasodilatory and antiplatelet properties that significantly improves maximal and pain-free walking distance in intermittent claudication, but is contraindicated in heart failure of any severity.

sections.name: Congenital heart disease and special topics

topics.title: Acyanotic congenital heart disease
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 82 (Congenital Heart Disease in Adult and Adolescent)

mustKnow.fact: Secundum atrial septal defect (ASD) is the most common adult ASD (accounting for 75% of cases), characterized by wide fixed splitting of the second heart sound and pulmonary flow murmur, amenable to transcatheter percutaneous device closure if adequate rims (>= 5 mm) exist.

Primum ASD occurs in the inferior interatrial septum near AV valves as a component of partial AV septal defect (AVSD), displaying marked left axis deviation on ECG and a cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet causing mitral regurgitation.
Sinus venosus ASD (superior type) is situated near the SVC-RA junction and is strongly associated with partial anomalous pulmonary venous return (PAPVR) of right upper pulmonary veins into the SVC.

Ventricular septal defect (VSD) classification comprises perimembranous (most common, 70%-80%), muscular (trabecular), inlet (AV canal type), and outlet/supracristal (doubly committed subarterial, predisposing to aortic valve prolapse and aortic regurgitation).

Significant left-to-right shunt warranting defect closure in ASD or VSD is defined by a pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio (Qp/Qs) >= 1.5:1 with right ventricular volume overload, provided pulmonary vascular resistance is < 3 to 5 Wood units.

Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) connects the proximal descending aorta to the roof of the main pulmonary artery, presenting with a continuous machinery murmur at the left infraclavicular area and wide pulse pressure.

Coarctation of the aorta typically occurs near the insertion of the ligamentum arteriosum, manifesting with upper extremity hypertension, radiofemoral pulse delay, rib notching (Roesler sign, ribs 3-8), and figure-3 sign on chest radiograph.
Cor triatriatum sinistrum is a rare congenital anomaly where the left atrium is divided into two chambers by a fibromuscular membrane, mimicking mitral stenosis with pulmonary venous congestion.

modules.name: Cyanotic and adult congenital heart disease

topics.title: Cyanotic and adult congenital heart disease
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 82 (Congenital Heart Disease in Adult and Adolescent)

mustKnow.fact: Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) consists of four anatomical components: large malaligned perimembranous VSD, right ventricular outflow tract obstruction (infundibular and valvular pulmonic stenosis), overriding aorta (< 50%), and concentric right ventricular hypertrophy.

Late complications in repaired adult TOF include severe chronic pulmonary regurgitation causing progressive RV dilation and dysfunction, requiring pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) when RV end-diastolic volume index exceeds 160 mL/m2 or end-systolic volume index exceeds 80 mL/m2.

Eisenmenger syndrome represents the irreversible progression of long-standing left-to-right shunts into severe pulmonary vascular remodeling, elevated PVR exceeding systemic resistance, shunt reversal to right-to-left, and central cyanosis.

Differential cyanosis (pink upper extremities with cyanotic, clubbed lower extremities) is pathognomonic of patent ductus arteriosus with Eisenmenger physiology and right-to-left shunting delivered distal to the left subclavian artery.

Transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA) features ventriculoarterial discordance (aorta arising from RV and pulmonary artery arising from LV), where the arterial switch operation (Jatene procedure) is the anatomical surgical repair of choice in neonates.

Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (l-TGA) features double discordance (atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance), where the morphological RV functions as the systemic pumping ventricle, leading to long-term systemic RV failure and high-grade AV block.

Fontan procedure provides single-ventricle palliation by routing systemic venous return directly to the pulmonary arteries without an intervening subpulmonary pumping chamber, complicated long-term by protein-losing enteropathy and plastic bronchitis.

Secondary erythrocytosis in cyanotic CHD is a physiologic compensatory response to chronic hypoxemia; therapeutic phlebotomy is indicated only for symptomatic hyperviscosity (hematocrit > 65%) with concurrent volume replacement to prevent microvascular occlusion.

modules.name: Heart disease in pregnancy and cardio-oncology

topics.title: Heart disease in pregnancy and cardio-oncology
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 84, 92 (Pregnancy and Heart Disease, Cardio-Oncology)

mustKnow.fact: Modified World Health Organization (mWHO) risk classification stratifies maternal cardiovascular risk during pregnancy from Class I (low risk, 2.5%-5%) to Class IV (extremely high risk, 40%-100% mortality/severe morbidity where pregnancy is strictly contraindicated).

mWHO Class IV conditions where pregnancy is contraindicated include severe pulmonary arterial hypertension of any cause, severe systemic ventricular dysfunction (LVEF < 30% or NYHA III-IV), severe native mitral stenosis, severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, and vascular Ehlers-Danlos.

Anticoagulation in pregnant women with mechanical prosthetic heart valves balances maternal and fetal risk: low-dose warfarin (<= 5 mg daily) can be continued in first trimester due to low embryopathy rate (< 3%), or switched to dose-adjusted LMWH with anti-Xa monitoring (target 0.8-1.2 IU/mL).

Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is an idiopathic heart failure presenting with LVEF < 45% toward the end of pregnancy or in the months following delivery, where bromocriptine (dopamine D2 agonist that blocks 16-kDa prolactin cleavage) enhances recovery.

Anthracycline cardiotoxicity (doxorubicin) is dose-dependent, irreversible type I cardiotoxicity mediated by topoisomerase II-beta poisoning and reactive oxygen species, with clinical heart failure incidence rising sharply above cumulative lifetime doses of 400 to 550 mg/m2.

Dexrazoxane is an intracellular iron-chelating agent and catalytic topoisomerase II inhibitor cardioprotectant approved for preventing anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity in patients requiring high cumulative doses.

Trastuzumab cardiotoxicity (HER2-targeted therapy) is dose-independent, reversible type II myocardial dysfunction without ultrastructural myocyte loss, manifesting as asymptomatic LVEF decline that typically recovers after drug interruption.

Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is defined by a relative decline in global longitudinal strain (GLS) > 15% from baseline or an absolute decrease in LVEF >= 10 percentage points to a value < 50%.

modules.name: Cardiac tumours and heart in systemic disease

topics.title: Cardiac tumours and heart in systemic disease
topics.book: Braunwald 12e Ch. 97, 98 (Cardiac Tumors and Rheumatic/Systemic Diseases)

mustKnow.fact: Cardiac myxoma is the most common primary cardiac tumor in adults (accounting for 50% of cases), typically arising from the fossa ovalis border in the left atrium (75%) and presenting with intracardiac obstruction, embolic phenomena, and constitutional symptoms.

Carney complex is an autosomal dominant syndrome caused by PRKAR1A mutations, combining recurrent cardiac myxomas, spotty skin pigmentation (lentigines), and endocrine tumors (primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease).

Papillary fibroelastoma is the most common primary tumor of cardiac valves (aortic and mitral valves), resembling a sea anemone on echocardiography with multiple papillary fronds and posing high embolic stroke risk requiring surgical excision.

Cardiac rhabdomyoma is the most frequent primary cardiac tumor in infants and children, strongly associated with tuberous sclerosis (mutations in TSC1/TSC2) and characterized by spontaneous regression.

Cardiac angiosarcoma is the most common primary malignant cardiac tumor in adults, typically located in the right atrium and pericardium with early hemorrhagic pericardial effusion, tamponade, and widespread metastases.

Metastatic tumors to the heart are 20 to 40 times more frequent than primary cardiac tumors, most often originating from lung cancer, breast cancer, melanoma (which has the highest propensity for myocardial metastasis), and lymphoma.

Carcinoid heart disease occurs in patients with neuroendocrine tumors and hepatic metastases due to circulating vasoactive serotonin (5-HT), causing pathognomonic plaque-like fibrous thickening of tricuspid and pulmonic valves leading to severe tricuspid regurgitation.

Rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) involve the heart through pericarditis, myocarditis, accelerated coronary atherosclerosis, and Libman-Sacks endocarditis (verrucous, nonbacterial valvular lesions on both surfaces of mitral and aortic leaflets).
